title: What's a Seal Doing in the Stream?

collection.credit: NEW EVENTS — WHAT'S THAT DOING HERE? (WD-01 to WD-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)

ledger.why: the casting line (the roles carry it)

collection.description: A seal has come up the stream for a nap in the best water-filling spot: wait for it, or fill up elsewhere.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (name1) goes down to the stream to fill (his/her) water jar and finds the stream already occupied. A large, sleek, grey animal is lying across the shallows like a log, fast asleep, whiskers twitching. It has come all the way up from the sea, apparently for a nap, and it is using the best water-filling spot in the village as a bed.

choices.label: Wait for It to Wake Up

a.name: Answer A
a.text: (name1) sits on the bank. The seal snores. A small crowd gathers. The seal snores on. Eventually it opens one eye, looks at all the villagers staring at it, sighs a long, deep, put-upon sigh, and flops its way back down the stream to the sea, as if to say that some people can't let anyone rest. Everyone fills their jars at once.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (name1) tiptoes upstream and fills (his/her) jar at a different spot. When (he/she) comes back an hour later, the seal has gone, leaving a large seal-shaped dent in the mud. (name1) shows it to the children. By the evening the story has grown, and the seal was apparently as big as a canoe and could talk.
